# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Mar 19, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's focus was on addressing critical CI flakiness, with significant progress made in identifying root causes and proposing fixes for several long-standing test failures. Discussions also continued on improving the initial EL sync UX and correctness for `op-node`.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS
No completed work was reported for this period.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **Dependency Updates**: A new pull request was opened to bump the `google.golang.org/grpc` dependency from 1.74.2 to 1.79.3 in the `/op-signer` module. [#573](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/573)

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
- **CI Flakiness in Interop Proofs**: Two new issues were opened to track persistent flakiness in the `TestChallengerPlaysGame` and `TestProposer` tests within the `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs` package. Both tests are reported to hang indefinitely, leading to 2-hour subtest timeouts in CI. [#19672](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19672), [#19673](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19673)

## ACTIVE ISSUES
- **Initial EL Sync UX and Correctness for op-node**: Discussions continued on the `op-node`'s initial EL sync behavior. The core issue is that after initial EL sync, the `op-node` incorrectly sets safe and finalized heads to the unsafe head, rather than relying on the L1 finalization gadget. A proposal to set safe/finalized to the unsafe head minus the sequencer window (~12 hours) was highlighted as a good balance between correctness and user experience, requiring derivation of roughly 12 hours of data. Other options, such as setting safe/finalized to genesis or providing them via an external source, were also discussed. [#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/17631)
- **Review kona-interop block hash oracle**: The discussion revolved around ensuring an integration/acceptance test exists to verify block hash lookups prior to the current history window. It was noted that an existing action test covers this, and the goal is to potentially move this to an acceptance test that works with `op-supernode` and can generate sufficient chain history, possibly using L1 time travel. [#18288](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/18288)
- **Non-terminating CI job: memory-all-opn-op-geth**: This issue was reopened due to the `memory-all-opn-op-geth` job hanging again. The `TestChallengerPlaysGame` and `TestProposer` tests in `interop/proofs` were identified as hitting 2-hour subtest timeouts. Root causes for these specific test hangs were identified: `TestChallengerPlaysGame` was a collateral victim of `TestProposer` hanging, and `TestProposer`'s hang was due to `FailNow` being called inside `testify.Eventually` goroutines, causing them to block indefinitely. Fixes involving package isolation and replacing fatal assertions with error-returning variants were proposed. [#19563](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19563)
- **Flaky: TestInteropFaultProofs_ConsolidateValidCrossChainMessage**: The root cause for this flaky test was identified as a race condition in `op-service/testutils/tcpproxy/proxy.go`. Specifically, `handleConn` holding a mutex while dialing upstream could lead to untracked connections when `Close()` was called, causing `wg.Wait()` to hang. A fix was proposed to release the mutex before dialing and check for `p.stopped` before registering connections. [#19656](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/19656)
